title: Lemma 4 (D-lim): Peircean limit-pragmatism is absorbed by redefinition, begging the question

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The 'Against D-lim' argument concludes that, 'made precise,' Peircean limit-pragmatism IS a special case of the proposed account (objectivity relative to the framework encoding the limit-conditions). This is definitional annexation, not refutation. It assumes the Peircean must specify truth-tracking inquiry-policies as a set 𝓜 *assessed by agent-invariant criteria* — but the Peircean's point is that 'truth'/'truth-tracking' are *defined by* the limit, not assessed against a prior agent-invariant standard. The lemma thus presupposes the endorsement-independent standard it aims to vindicate (begging the question), or wins only verbally by relabeling.

Fix: use the standard convergence objection — 'the limit of inquiry' presupposes a metric/convergence structure on belief states not fixed by endorsement; if the Peircean denies such structure the limit is undefined, if she grants it she has granted an endorsement-independent standard. Argue this on the Peircean's own definition of truth-at-the-limit.
